title: Clarifi Health POC playbook and success criteria
content:
Summary:
This doc is the working playbook for the Clarifi Health POC. Goal: prove that Redwood can serve Clarifi’s clinical summarization and triage assistant with privacy-preserving deployment (VPC/private) while meeting latency, throughput, and hallucination controls. This is a pragmatic, 6-week hands-on POC focused on engineering validation and a short pilot for a single clinical workflow (inbound teletriage notes -> structured summary + risk flags).

Scope (what we will demo):
- Secure private deployment (Clarifi VPC) of Redwood Private control plane + model runtime in Clarifi's AWS account or on-prem node (customer preference to test both dedicated and private modes).
- Two core features: 1) condensed clinical summarization (350–600 char summaries), 2) triage flagging (binary high/medium/low risk + rationale).
- Integration prototype with Clarifi staging EMR (FHIR bundle ingest via sample dataset). Not full production integration.

Non-goals:
- Full HIPAA attestation or SOC2 ramp (we will use existing Redwood compliance artifacts, but certification work is out of scope).
- Multi-department rollout, enterprise SSO, or billing integration.

Customer contacts:
- Laila Rahman — CTO, Clarifi Health (primary technical sponsor)
- Marcus Lee — Product Manager, Clarifi (use-case owner)
- Security reviewer: Priya Anand (Clarifi InfoSec)

Redwood leads:
- SE lead / POC owner: Ava Chen
- Runtime engineer: Ravi Patel
- Infra & private deploy SME: Tomás Müller
- Eval / quality lead: Mariana Lopez

Success criteria (must-pass items) - quantitative:
1) Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end latency for summarization requests < 800ms on sized workload (see load below). p50 < 220ms.
2) Throughput: sustained 60 req/s for summarization (single region, dedicated capacity) with service-level autoscaling triggers validated.
3) Accuracy / hallucination guard: <= 5% major hallucination rate against the curated eval set (50 clinical notes). Major hallucination = incorrect diagnosis or medication invented that is not in notes.
4) Triage precision: >= 85% precision for high-risk flags on the labeled test set (n=200).
5) Data isolation: verified that no logs leave Clarifi VPC and all persistent artifacts encrypted (customer-provided KMS key).
6) Cost target: inference cost for summarization configured to < $0.10 per 1k tokens equivalent for steady-state workload with batching and KV cache enabled (validated by Redwood Optimize recommendations).

Success criteria - qualitative:
- Product team signs off that summaries are "actionable" and reduce manual triage time in a quick usability run (3 clinicians, <15 minute session each).
- Deployable config artifact for Clarifi (Terraform + runbook) delivered and validated in their dev account.

Acceptance tests (how we validate):
- Acceptance test #1: End-to-end demo with 30 representative notes (staging). Run and capture latency percentiles and model outputs. Verify acceptance criteria 1&2. Ticket: JIRA-PS-271-AT1.
- Acceptance test #2: Eval-run on labeled set (200 cases) to compute hallucination and triage precision. Generate a short report with examples of failures. Ticket: JIRA-PS-271-AT2.
- Acceptance test #3: Security runbook validation with Clarifi InfoSec: confirm KMS integration, no plaintext logs, and IAM least privilege. Ticket: JIRA-PS-271-SEC.

Minimum environment & data requirements:
- Clarifi will provide a de-identified sample of 500 teletriage notes in FHIR JSON (fields list attached) plus mapping docs. If de-id not ready, use synthetic generator (we will provide script).
- Customer staging AWS account with VPC peering route and a customer-managed KMS key for encryption-at-rest (required for Private).
- Allowlist of IPs for temporary SSH/management access (per Clarifi policy) for the POC window.

Deployment options to test (we will deliver 2 configs):
1) Redwood Private (VPC) – control plane in Redwood, runtime in Clarifi's cloud (preferred for data isolation).
2) Redwood Dedicated in Redwood-managed infra with VPC egress controls (to show tradeoffs).
Notes: clarify support for HSM/KMS and audit-log forwarding in week 1 workshop.

Workshop plan (Week 0 kickoff + two technical sessions):
- Kickoff (2 hours): goals, scope, data requirements, access checklist, security baseline, success metrics, timeline. Attendees: Clarifi PM + InfoSec + infra + 3 Redwood leads.
- Tech session A (half day): sample dataset walkthrough, ingest pipeline, schema mapping, transformation scripts, local inference smoke tests.
- Tech session B (half day): deployment variants, autoscaling policy review, observability (console walkthrough), and failover plan.
- Clinician session (remote, 90 minutes): guided usability with 3 clinicians, capture qualitative feedback + time-on-task.

6-week timeline (high level):
Week 0: Kickoff + access + dataset ETA
Week 1: Private deployment prototype (single node) + smoke tests
Week 2: Integration with staging EMR + schema validation
Week 3: Model config iteration + eval run #1, tuning prompts and safety wrappers
Week 4: Performance tuning (batching, KV cache) + autoscale tests
Week 5: Clinician usability sessions + security runbook review
Week 6: Final acceptance tests, handoff artifacts, exec readout

Roles & responsibilities:
- Clarifi infra: provide staging account, KMS key, sample data, and a pager for access windows.
- Clarifi InfoSec: review runbook, perform the security acceptance checklist.
- Redwood SE: lead deploy, run tests, iterate prompts & safety rules.
- Redwood Infra: build Terraform and deployment artifacts; provide monitoring dashboards.

Evaluation & data collection plan:
- We'll store all eval inputs/outputs in Clarifi staging S3 with encryption. Only aggregated metrics and redacted failure examples will be shared outside Clarifi account.
- Generate evaluation reports: latency summary, hallucination examples, triage confusion matrix, token-cost estimate.
- Quick A/B: baseline (open Llama-variant) vs tuned quantized variant (Redwood recommended) to show cost/quality tradeoffs.

Sample prompts & safety wrapper notes (engineering reference):
- Summarization prompt: "You are a concise clinical summarizer. Given the clinician note below, produce a 2–4 sentence summary focusing on problem, vitals, medications mentioned, and next steps. Do not infer new medications or diagnoses. If information is missing, say 'insufficient evidence'."
- Safety wrapper: post-process to drop any entity suggested not present in the source. Flag as "possible hallucination" and return supporting evidence lines.

Open questions / risks:
- Q1: Clarifi licensing reqs for model weights if we recommend a specific open model. (Owner: Mariana)
- Q2: De-identification adequacy (customer to confirm). Risk: PII leakage during eval if de-id incomplete. Mitigation: synthetic fallback + additional filtering.
- Risk: Observability noise—Clarifi wants token-level logging blocked. We must validate that usage telemetry can be aggregated without raw token retention.

Deliverables for handoff:
- Terraform module and runbook (deploy/rollback/playbook)
- Eval report with metrics and failure examples
- Short exec slide deck (3–5 slides) showing pass/fail on must-pass success criteria and recommended next steps
- Implementation recommendations (batching, cached prefixes, quantization profile)

Quick todo / action items (first 10 days):
- [Ava] Confirm Clarifi staging account access and KMS (by 2024-11-08).
- [Tomás] Prepare private-deploy reference Terraform module (by 2024-11-11).
- [Mariana] Create initial labeled eval set and eval rubric (by 2024-11-12).
- [Ravi] Baseline latency run with default config using sample dataset (by 2024-11-13).
- [Clarifi: Marcus] Provide de-identified sample (500 notes) or approve synthetic generator (by 2024-11-10).

Notes / references:
- Related internal doc: CONFLUENCE-CH-154 has Clarifi contractual slack notes and baseline SOW language.
- Temp GH: GH-PR-842 contains the early terraform snippet we’ll iterate on.
- Slack thread: slack:#solutions-clarifi-thread for day-to-day coordination.

Working status & expected blockers:
- Status: resourcing confirmed; infra engineer assigned; awaiting Clarifi staging access and de-id dataset.
- Expected blocker: InfoSec may require additional audits for HSM; prioritize KMS-only path first.

Appendix: quick eval rubric (short):
- Hallucination severity: major / minor / cosmetic
- Triage label mapping: high (requires immediate action), medium (same-day), low (routine)
- Clinician acceptability: binary "actionable / not actionable" + free-text notes

If anything in this doc needs to change before the kickoff, flag in the Slack thread and update the Confluence stub. This is intentionally lightweight — the purpose is to get a running POC that validates the three pillars: privacy (VPC/KMS), performance (latency/throughput), and output reliability (low hallucination + precise triage flags).
